tasks.short: Replenish laboratory supplies before shortages or expiry

steps.what: Verify laboratory supplies, expiration dates and upcoming chemical requirements
Compare verified supplies with thresholds and prepare purchase lines
Check chemical suitability and purchase the approved laboratory supplies

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} laboratory inventory system to compare verified stock and expiry data with chemist-approved thresholds and populate {PROCUREMENT} draft lines. Physical stock checks, threshold decisions, chemical grade and storage suitability remain with the chemist before purchase.
tasks.previous_blocker: Threshold comparisons and re-entry recur after stock and expiry checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Native inventory alerts and requisition templates can apply explicit dates, units and quantities without selecting experimental substitutes.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded consumption, uncertain demand and chemically unsuitable substitutions.
tasks.human_edge: Know the required purity, method compatibility and safe storage constraints.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive comparison and entry, with unchanged scientific purchasing responsibility.

reach.learn: Reconcile container identity, usable quantity and expiry without guessing

evidence.claim: Rule-based inventory comparisons and draft requisitions are plausible model knowledge; the digest does not document this chemical replenishment design or measure its savings.

assumptions: Boundary is chemist replenishment checking, draft preparation and purchasing; excludes delivery, disposal and laboratory experiments.

Chemist produces item and container identity, usable quantity and unit, expiry date, chemical grade, required specification, approved minimum/target quantities, lead time, supplier and storage constraints in s1. Its full 45 hours include physical verification, threshold choice and field capture.
Native laboratory inventory configuration is tested first. Missing expiry, unit mismatch, stale counts or unapproved substitutions stop automated preparation and return to manual reconciliation.
No existing system runtime earns a saving; only the chemist's 25-hour comparison and entry component changes.
Five additional focal hours cover threshold reviews and stock exceptions. Two technician hours for additional stock-record correction are disclosed separately, not treated as free transferred work.
unknowns: Purchasing permissions and hazardous chemical controls
Proportion of one-off versus repeat supplies
research_questions: Do verified stock and expiry fields reduce net replenishment effort after capture and exception handling?

already_counted.description: Physical stock checks, threshold decisions and brief capture
Suitability, storage and final purchase review

incremental.description: Threshold maintenance and replenishment exception audits

approvals.approved_version: Exact chemical identity, grade, specification, supplier, quantity, price and delivery/storage details; substitution or quantity changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+0+30=75, gross=25, focal incremental=5, central net=20. High requires repeat chemicals with current verified stock fields and genuine manual comparison/entry today. Low retains all manual preparation for stale or one-off records plus upkeep. Physical verification and scientific suitability decisions retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The chemist may spend less time on repeat replenishment entry while retaining stock verification and scientific purchase decisions.
reach: Agree stock-record correction responsibilities with chemical technicians
role.ambitious_version: A chemist with traceable replenishment drafts who retains control over chemical suitability and laboratory needs.
